The one-year view of the reserves: Merz and Wuthrich's claims development result

Source: R/reserving_one_year_munich.R
merz_wuthrich.Rd

The standard error of the claims development result (CDR) of the next year: how much the chain ladder's ultimate can move in one year, as the year's claims emerge and the factors are estimated again. It is the reserve risk over one year that Solvency II measures, against Mack's standard error of the reserves until they are all paid.

Usage

merz_wuthrich(triangle, sigma = c("log-linear", "Mack"))

Arguments

triangle

A numeric matrix of cumulative claims: one row per origin period, oldest first, and one column per development period, with NA for the future. A data frame is converted with as.matrix(); see as_triangle to build one from a table of claims.

sigma

How \(\sigma\) is found for a period with a single link ratio: "log-linear" or "Mack".

Value

An object of class netsimr_reserve: a list with by_origin, a data frame with each origin's latest claims, ultimate, IBNR, the standard error of its one-year CDR and Mack's standard error until ultimate; total, the same for all origins; and chain_ladder, the chain ladder they come from.

Details

The formulas of Merz and Wuthrich (2008) hold for the volume-weighted chain ladder of every link ratio without a tail, which the function fits; with Mack's \(\sigma_j\) and the shares \(\alpha_j = C_{I-j,j} / \sum_{i \le I-j} C_{ij}\), the mean squared error of each origin's CDR is its next year's process error, \(\hat C_{iJ}^2 \hat\sigma_j^2 / (\hat f_j^2 C_{ij})\), plus the error of the factors, which counts each later factor's error by the share \(\alpha\) of its estimate that the year's claims change; the total adds the correlation of the origins. The results match the ChainLadder package's CDR(), and for the Taylor and Ashe triangle Merz and Wuthrich's paper.

References

Merz, M. and Wuthrich, M. V. (2008). Modelling the claims development result for solvency purposes. CAS E-Forum, Fall 2008, 542-568.

See also

chain_ladder for Mack's standard error until ultimate, and bootstrap_chain_ladder.

Examples

merz_wuthrich(taylor_ashe_triangle, sigma = "Mack")
